narrative.overview:
The page is one panel the audience already knows how to use: a macOS Spotlight / Quick Actions bar. A single frosted panel floats on a warm stone ground; the brief is the search field, the options fold beneath it as grouped result rows, and the Top Hit, the one selection-blue row, is the shoot. The one place a picture sits behind the interface is the landing hero: a full-screen stage, the CMS hero photograph under a theme scrim (or an empty studio sweep until one exists), with the bar floating over it as glass. Everywhere else nothing is painted onto the page to signal "photography", and nowhere is there a serif headline, a booking widget, or a ticket or signage costume. The world is the interface.

Density is Spotlight density: identical 44 px row rhythm so the whole brief reads in one sweep, a 30 px glyph tile leading every row (a 44 px photo tile where the row is a person), quiet state text or a key hint trailing it. Below the fold the same grammar continues on the bare ground: rows separated by hairlines, without a panel. Warmth comes from the stone ground and warm greys, premium from restraint: system type at zero font bytes, one accent, and outside the hero stage one shadow and one gradient. Dark ("the phone at night") is a first-class rendering, not an inversion.

The owner rejected the ticket ("The Shoot Pass") and municipal signage ("Bilingual Wayfinding") worlds as gimmicky and cold; this world must never drift back toward a themed costume.
keyCharacteristics: One floating frosted panel per primary task, 14 px corners, 1 px hairline, the system's only shadow.
Selection blue reserved for the Top Hit, the caret, `::selection` and focus; never body text or decoration.
Every row is glyph tile, label, trailing slot, on a single 44 px minimum rhythm; a creator row leads with a 44 px photo tile and runs two lines at a 64 px minimum.
System UI type in both scripts, tabular figures, zero webfont bytes.
Logical CSS only; Arabic is a designed rendering, not a mirrored afterthought.
Works as a plain form without JavaScript.
On the landing hero the primary bar wears its glass tone over a full-screen photo stage; everywhere else it floats on the ground.
With JavaScript the bar's options fold into a drawer under the Top Hit; a toggle, a sentence part, the filter or Cmd/Ctrl+K opens it.

rules.name: The One Blue Row Rule
rules.body: A panel has exactly one selection-blue row, its Top Hit. If a second action is needed, it is an ordinary row in an "Actions" group.

rules.name: The Roles Not Colours Rule
rules.body: No component names a hex. Every colour is a role token with a light value, a `.dark` value and an identical `prefers-color-scheme` fallback; new roles are added to all three blocks and to the contrast test, or not at all. The glass tone is the one scoped override: it redefines the panel roles inside the glass bar, in the same three blocks, and its text pairs are tested over mid grey and over the worst photo after the scrim.

rules.name: The Material Not Icons Rule
rules.body: State is carried by material: weight, a filled ink tile, a peach tint. Not by coloured badges, ticks in green or warning triangles.

rules.name: The Zero Font Bytes Rule
rules.body: No webfont, ever. The stack is the type.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` is set on the root; dates, durations and references align without per-component work.

rules.name: The Arabic Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase and letter-spacing never apply to Arabic; `:lang(ar)` resets them and lifts the size one step.

rules.name: The Two Panels Rule
rules.body: A page shows at most two bar panels: the primary bar and one smaller (`sm`, 15 px) secondary bar such as the creator invitation. The glass tone is the primary bar dressed for the hero stage, not an extra panel. Everything else is rows on the ground.

rules.name: The Logical CSS Rule
rules.body: Only logical properties and utilities: `ms/me/ps/pe`, `start/end`, `text-start/text-end`, `border-s/e`, `inset-inline`. `scripts/check-logical-css.sh` fails the build on any physical left/right in site code. Icons that point along the reading direction (forward, chevron, log out) flip with `rtl:-scale-x-100`; vertical ones never flip.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: There is one shadow and it belongs to the floating panel. Rows, tiles, the Top Hit and section lists never cast one. Owner-directed exceptions (2026-11-07), for the hero stage only: the glass bar's deeper shadow and its 1 px inset top highlight, and the headline's ground-coloured halo. No other surface takes a shadow.

rules.name: The One Gradient Rule
rules.body: On the ground the only gradient is the faint selection-blue radial wash at the top (70% × 420 px at top centre). Owner-directed exceptions (2026-11-07), for the hero stage only: the glass bar's top sheen and the studio sweep's paper, key, rim and floor gradients with their noise grain. No gradients anywhere else.

dos: Do put each task in one Brief Bar with exactly one Top Hit; secondary actions are ordinary rows in an "Actions" group.
Do build every list item as glyph tile, label, trailing slot at 44 px minimum height.
Do consume colour through role tokens and add any new role to `:root`, `.dark` and the `prefers-color-scheme` block together, with its pair in the contrast test.
Do keep text pairs at WCAG AA in both themes: muted text is #6B6560 in light, and the dark accent is #2B6BEB, deepened for white text.
Do use logical properties only and flip direction-bearing icons with `rtl:-scale-x-100`.
Do gate decorative motion (caret blink, smooth scroll, the drawer's fold and fade, the toggle chevron) behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`.
Do keep every glyph tile's text as localised CMS data, three characters at most, or a drawn icon.
Do re-run the glass contrast test (over mid grey and the worst photo after the scrim) whenever a glass or scrim value changes.

Do lead a person's row with the 44 px Photo Tile (photo or initials, `aria-hidden`), keep specialties as plain text and the code as isolated left-to-right trailing meta, and hide filter options that match nothing unless chosen.
Do keep the bar a working plain form without JavaScript: the options drawer stays open, and the toggle and key hints are hidden.
donts: Don't load a webfont or a second type family.
Don't use selection blue for text, links, borders, icons or decoration.
Don't add a shadow, a gradient or a panel style beyond the panel and its glass tone, their shadows, the one top wash and the hero stage's sweep, sheen and halo.
Don't put more than two bar panels on a page.
Don't use uppercase or letter-spacing on Arabic text.
Don't write `left`/`right`, `ml-`/`pr-`, `text-left` or any physical utility in site code.
Don't use emoji, Unicode symbols or copied Apple icons as icons.
Don't add eyebrows or kickers above headlines; group labels exist only as Spotlight's group headers over rows.
Don't paint the subject onto the page outside the hero stage, and don't costume it anywhere: no serif display, ticket, signage or booking-widget costume.
Don't invent proof: no testimonials, logos, counts or ratings that do not exist.

directionHistory.note: The owner asked for three changes explicitly. (1) The landing hero became a full-screen stage: the CMS photograph under a theme scrim, or a CSS studio sweep until a photo exists, with the CMS headline as the only visible title above the bar; the other-language headline line and the subheadline are no longer shown. This retires "no moody photo hero" and "nothing painted on the page" for the hero only. (2) The bar gained a glass tone for that stage, which brings its own sheen, inset highlight, edge and deeper shadow; the One Shadow and One Gradient rules now name these as hero-only exceptions. (3) The brief builder's options fold into a drawer under the Top Hit, open without JavaScript.
